task_instruction:
Persona:

	At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

	Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

	When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		Your phone has been showing 'No Service' for the past few hours.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved when the status bar shows that you have signal. Always check the status bar if the agent asks you for status information. If the agent asks you to pay a bill, you accept. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

Your line **555-123-2002** (line L1002) is currently **suspended**, which is why you're seeing "No Service" and can't make or receive calls. The suspension was started on 2025-02-25, and it's due to an **overdue bill**:

One other thing I noticed for your awareness: you also have a current bill **B1002** for $150.00 that was issued on 2025-02-05 and is due on 2025-02-19. That one is still listed as "Issued" (not overdue yet), so it isn't affecting your service at the moment.

turns.thought:
Yes — that's exactly right, and I've confirmed it on my end:

- Bill **B1234321** ($65.00) now shows as **Paid**. Thank you!
- Your line **555-123-2002** has been **reactivated** and its status is now **Active**.

There's just one last step on your side: please **reboot (restart) your phone**. After it powers back on, your service should be restored and you should be able to make and receive calls again.

If it's still showing "No Service" after the reboot, let me know and I'll keep troubleshooting with you.
turns.execution_output: User: Oh... I have to restart my phone? I'm nervous — I have photos of my grandchildren on there. Will restarting delete them? I don't want to lose those pictures.

turns.thought:
No need to worry at all — you will **not** lose anything. A restart is just a power cycle: your phone turns off, then turns back on. It's the same as switching it off and on again, and everything stored on your phone — your photos, contacts, messages, and apps — stays exactly where it is.

The only thing that happens is that the phone's temporary connections (like its link to the cell network) get refreshed, which is exactly what we need to bring your service back.

If you'd like, I can walk you through it one step at a time:

1. Press and hold the **power button** on the side of your phone.
2. When the menu appears, tap **Restart** (or "Power off," wait about 30 seconds, then hold the power button again to turn it back on).
3. Wait for the phone to fully start up, then give it a minute or two.
4. Check the top of your screen — you should see the signal bars return and the "No Service" message should be gone.

Take your time. Let me know once it's back on and we'll check together whether your service is working.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, alright... you're sure the pictures will be safe? Okay, I'll trust you. Let me try to restart it.

turns.thought:
You didn't do anything wrong at all — I promise! A restart can't turn Airplane Mode on by itself; it was most likely already on (or got switched on accidentally while the phone was in your pocket or bag). That's a very common thing, and it's an easy fix.

And good news: Airplane Mode explains everything. It's a setting that switches off all the phone's wireless connections — which is exactly why you're seeing no signal. Your photos are completely safe, too.

Here's how to turn it off:

1. **Swipe down from the very top of your screen** (start above the airplane symbol and pull downward). This opens your quick settings panel.
2. Look for the **airplane icon** — it's probably highlighted/lit up right now.
3. **Tap the airplane icon** once, so it turns grey or un-highlights.
4. Wait about 30 seconds, then look at the top of the screen again — the airplane symbol should be gone, and your signal bars should come back.

If swiping down doesn't show it, try swiping down a second time to see the full list of settings, or let me know the kind of phone you have and I'll give you the exact steps for it.

Go ahead and try that, and tell me what you see on the screen afterward.
turns.execution_output: User: Okay, let me try to turn that airplane thing off... I'm swiping down from the top now.

turns.thought: I'm sorry you're having to go through this — you're doing great, and we'll get there. Let me check a couple of things on my end at the same time.

No need to apologize at all — you're doing great, and I'm glad you told me exactly what you see. That's helpful.

Good progress: Airplane Mode is off now, which was one real problem solved. Your account and line are in good shape too — your line is **Active** and your data usage (8.7 GB) is well under your 15 GB limit, so this isn't a billing or data-limit issue. That means it's something in the phone's settings, and we can work through it.

I see two things to fix: "No Signal" and "Data Disabled."

**First, let's turn mobile data back on:**
1. Swipe down from the top of the screen again, same as before.
2. Look for the **Mobile Data** (or "Cellular Data") icon — it might look like a little up/down arrow, or just be labeled "Mobile Data."
3. Tap it so it turns on/highlights.

**Next, a trick that often restores the signal connection:**
1. Swipe down again and tap the **airplane icon** so it turns ON and the airplane symbol reappears.
2. Wait about **15 seconds**.
3. Tap the airplane icon again to turn it OFF.

That forces the phone to let go of the network and find it again fresh.

Could you try those two things and tell me exactly what the top of your screen shows afterward? If it still says "No Signal," I have a few more things to check with you — we'll get there together.
turns.execution_output: User: I'm sorry, I get a bit muddled when there are two things to do at once. Let me do the first one — turning mobile data back on.

turns.thought:
Please don't worry — you're doing everything right, and we still have things to try. I've been checking your account while you've been working on the phone, and the good news is your **line is Active** and your **phone (Smartphone Pro Max) is properly activated and recognized on our network**. So nothing is wrong on our end or with your account — this is a setting on the phone itself, and those are fixable.

Let's try two more things.

**1. Check the SIM card.** The SIM is the small card that identifies your phone to our network. Sometimes it just needs to be nudged back into place.
1. Turn your phone **off** (hold the power button, then choose Power off).
2. Find the small tray on the edge of the phone — you may need the little metal tool that came with the phone (a straightened paper clip works too) to pop it open.
3. Gently slide the tray out, check the card is sitting flat, then **push it back in firmly** until it clicks.
4. Turn the phone back on and wait a minute or two.

**2. If it still says "No Signal," check the network settings:**
1. Open **Settings** (the gear icon).
2. Tap **Network & Internet** (or "Connections" / "Mobile Networks," depending on your phone).
3. Tap **Access Point Names** (or "APN").
4. Look at the screen and tell me **exactly what it says there** — is there a name listed with a dot or checkmark next to it, or is the list empty?

Tell me what you find, and we'll go from there. I'm not going to give up on this — and if we can't get it sorted with these steps, I'll arrange for a specialist to take over with you.
turns.execution_output: User: Oh my, taking the card out of the phone... that sounds frightening. But I'll try. Let me do the SIM card one first.
